ch38.d.show: Real part $\mathrm{Re}\,\psi$, probability density $|\psi|^2$, or both
ch38.d.k0: Central wave number $k_0$ of the components; the momentum is $p = \hbar k_0$
ch38.k.goal.build: Adding plane waves with slightly different wave numbers gives a localised wave packet
ch38.k.goal.move: The packet moves at the group velocity $\hbar k_0/m$, the speed of a classical particle with the same momentum
ch38.k.obs.one: One plane wave: $|\psi|^2$ is the same everywhere; the position is completely unknown
ch38.k.obs.more: More components (larger $\Delta k$) make a narrower packet (smaller $\Delta x$)
ch38.k.obs.product: $\Delta x\,\Delta k \approx 1/2$: position and wave number cannot both be narrowed (uncertainty)
ch38.k.obs.group: The packet (|ψ|²) keeps pace with the classical particle; the crests of Re ψ move at half that speed (phase velocity)
ch38.k.obs.spread: Narrower packets spread faster as they move (dispersion of a free particle)
ch38.k.assume.electron: Particle: a free electron in one dimension. $k_0$ = 10 nm⁻¹ means 3.8 eV kinetic energy and 1.16 nm/fs
ch38.k.assume.period: Equally spaced components repeat the packet every 42 nm (finitely many components); $\Delta x$ is taken over one repeat
ch38.d.eK: Kinetic energy $K$ of the electron (accelerating voltage × $e$)
ch38.d.goal.lambda: Every particle has a wave nature with wavelength $\lambda = h/p$
ch38.d.goal.scale: The wave nature shows only when the wavelength is comparable to the structure it meets (atom spacing, slits)
ch38.d.obs.electron: Electrons at 54–100 eV: wavelength close to the atom spacing (about 0.2 nm), so crystals diffract them (Davisson-Germer)
ch38.d.obs.neutron: Thermal neutrons (2200 m/s): 0.18 nm, used to study crystal structures
ch38.d.obs.c60: C₆₀ at 220 m/s: 2.5 pm, far smaller than the molecule (1 nm), yet interference has been observed with gratings
ch38.d.obs.ball: Baseball at 40 m/s: $\lambda \approx 10^{-34}$ m, twenty orders of magnitude below a nucleus; no wave behaviour can be seen
ch38.d.obs.energy: Larger momentum (heavier or faster) means a shorter wavelength
ch38.d.assume.rel: Momentum from the relativistic formula (about 0.5% different for a 10 keV electron)
ch38.d.assume.refs: Reference sizes are rough: nucleus 10⁻¹⁴ m, atom spacing 0.2 nm, visible light 500 nm, hair 0.1 mm. Grey discs in the lower picture: atoms 0.2 nm apart
